column2: Which hepatitis B marker calls for dedicated dialysis equipment and supplies in a chronic hemodialysis unit?
column7: A patient positive for hepatitis B surface antigen needs HBV isolation precautions, including dedicated equipment. Anti-HBs indicates antibody rather than current surface antigen.

column2: Which contamination route explains why hand hygiene follows routine removal of intact-looking gloves?
column3: Glove exterior to the wearer's skin
column5: Bare hand to an open sterile pack
column6: Reusable equipment to the next patient
column7: The act of removing gloves can transfer material from the outside of the gloves to hands. The other routes call for precautions at other points in care.

column2: A sharps box is above its fill line beside the chair. Which replacement setup is appropriate?
column5: Open puncture-resistant tray beside the chair
column6: Lined waste bin at the bedside
column7: Replace the full container with a closable, puncture-resistant container placed upright and close to the point of use. A distant container does not meet the point-of-use principle.

column2: At turnover, which items from the station go to the area for cleaning and disinfection?
column3: Reusable clamps and blood pressure cuffs
column4: Unopened gauze packs and reusable clamps
column5: Blood pressure cuffs and wrapped syringes
column6: Sealed tape rolls and unopened gauze packs
column7: Send reusable clamps and cuffs for cleaning and disinfection. Discard single-use supplies that entered the station, even if the packaging is intact.

column2: The previous patient has left and dried blood remains on the chair arm. How should turnover proceed?
column3: Clean the soil, then disinfect before setup
column4: Disinfect the arm, then clean before setup
column5: Place supplies, then clean and disinfect
column6: Clean the arm, then disinfect after seating
column7: Visible soil must be removed before disinfection. Complete the label's wet contact time and let surfaces dry before bringing the next patient or clean supplies to the station.

column2: Wiping starts at 10:00. A chair arm is fully wetted at 10:02. When does its three-minute contact time end?
column7: The arm needs three minutes of continuous wet contact beginning at 10:02. Time spent applying product elsewhere does not count toward that interval.

column2: Which EXIT sign meets OSHA's minimum dimensions for both letter height and principal stroke width?
column7: OSHA requires EXIT letters at least 6 inches high with principal strokes at least 3/4 inch wide. Both dimensions must meet the minimum.

column2: A drill log already lists each evacuee, exit and departure time. What else tracks patients relocated off-site?
column3: Name and location of the receiving site
column4: Name and number of the attending clinician
column7: The facility tracks patient locations during emergencies. When a patient is relocated, document the specific receiving facility or other destination.

column2: Which protection is required when blood splashes could reasonably reach the eyes, nose, and mouth?
column7: Use a mask with appropriate eye protection or a chin-length face shield when splashes may reach facial mucous membranes. Ordinary eyeglasses do not provide the required side protection.

column2: Which route is interrupted by using a designated medication preparation area separate from dialysis chairs?
column3: Blood from the chair to clean vials
column4: Blood from a shared cuff to another patient
column5: Blood from a used needle to the worker
column6: Blood from a dressing to nearby tubing
column7: The dedicated area separates clean medications and preparation supplies from patient treatment surfaces. Other precautions address shared equipment and sharps.

column2: While caring for an HBsAg-positive patient, which other patient can the technician cover during the same shift?
column4: Patient awaiting the first HBV vaccine dose
column6: New admission with unknown HBV status
column7: CDC permits one worker to care for infected and immune patients on the same shift. Protect susceptible patients by assigning their concurrent care to different staff. Unknown status requires assessment before making this assignment.

column2: A coworker removes station gloves. They are about to restock shared supplies. What reminder fits this transition?
column3: Clean hands before handling the packs
column5: Put on fresh gloves before stocking
column6: Clean hands at the next station
column7: Perform hand hygiene after removing gloves and before touching clean stock. Hand hygiene later would leave the shared shelf exposed during this task.

column2: A reusable cuff leaves a station. Its manufacturer permits a compatible surface disinfectant. How should staff prepare it for another patient?
column4: Disinfect tubing, replace the cuff pouch
column5: Clean cuff, disinfect visibly soiled areas
column7: Clean and disinfect the reusable cuff itself before its return to common use. Contamination need not be visible.

column2: All station surfaces are ready for use except the disinfected priming bucket. When may staff reconnect it?
column6: After the outside is wiped dry
column7: CDC directs staff to disinfect all bucket surfaces and allow the bucket to air-dry before reconnection. An exterior wipe or draining step alone does not complete the process.

column2: When selecting a handle to push a laundry cart, which height range should a technician use?
column7: OSHA's hospital laundry guidance places cart handles between waist and chest height. Grip the handles to push the cart.

column2: A patient says the treatment room is too cold. Other patients are comfortable. What should staff offer?
column3: Blanket placed clear of the access
column4: Reduced airflow across the entire room
column5: Blanket tucked around the access arm
column7: The facility should reasonably accommodate an individual patient's comfort needs. A blanket can help as long as staff can still see the access and bloodline connections.

column2: When are soap and water preferred over alcohol-based hand sanitizer during routine care?
column7: Use soap and water when hands are visibly soiled. Alcohol-based hand rub is generally preferred in most clinical situations when hands are not visibly dirty.

column2: Why should standard precautions apply before a patient's infection status has been established?
column3: Blood exposure can transmit undetected infection
column4: Isolation decisions do not depend on infection status
column5: All bloodborne infections require dedicated staffing
column6: Vaccination reduces the need for routine barriers
column7: Infection may be unrecognized, so staff apply standard precautions to all patients. Additional precautions depend on the specific infection or exposure risk.

column2: Which delivery belongs on the receiving side of the clinic's equipment reprocessing area?
column7: Items collected from patient stations enter the area for used equipment. Store cleaned devices and new supplies separately, and prepare medications away from used equipment.

column2: What does a positive hepatitis C RNA result change about routine dialysis station assignment by itself?
column3: No separate room or dedicated machine is needed
column4: Dedicated machine is needed in the shared room
column5: Separate room is needed with any available machine
column6: Separate room and dedicated staff are needed
column7: CDC does not require isolation or dedicated machines solely because of HCV infection. Continue dialysis infection control precautions used for all patients.

column2: At opening, the clinic's only defibrillation device is off-site for servicing. Which emergency preparedness requirement has not been met?
column7: The emergency plan must ensure a functioning AED or defibrillator is immediately available on the premises. Sending the only device for maintenance does not satisfy that requirement.

column2: At closing, a work surface may have been exposed to blood since cleaning. No spill is visible. When is decontamination due?
column3: By the end of the same shift
column5: When the station is next occupied
column7: OSHA calls for end-of-shift decontamination when the surface may have become contaminated since the last cleaning. Overt contamination warrants immediate action or action as soon as feasible.

column2: A leaking pipe affects a two-entrance corridor. Staff must leave before repairs. Where should access barriers go?
column3: At both approaches to the wet section
column4: At the pipe and the nearest floor drain
column5: At the supply valve and the repair cart
column6: At the leak and the nearest doorway
column7: When an unsafe walking surface cannot be corrected immediately, it must be guarded against use. Blocking both approaches keeps people off the affected section until it is safe.

column2: A nearby chemical release leads officials to order patients and staff to stay indoors. Which clinic procedure applies?
column7: The facility emergency plan must address when patients, staff, and volunteers shelter in place. An evacuation route is for a different response.

column2: A blood-filled needle punctures a technician's skin. Which first aid applies before prompt reporting and evaluation?
column7: Wash a puncture with soap and water, then report promptly and obtain evaluation. Flushing with water or saline is first aid for a splash to the eye.

column2: What does repeated HBsAg testing add to the care of dialysis patients susceptible to hepatitis B?
column6: Confirm that a past infection resolved
column7: Repeated HBsAg testing can detect a newly infected patient. Anti-HBs testing instead checks the antibody response to vaccination.

column2: A patient holds pressure at a separate chair after needle removal. When should staff disinfect that chair and its armrests?
column4: At the next treatment shift change
column5: At the end of the treatment day
column6: When a dressing leaves a visible stain
column7: A separate chair used while a patient achieves hemostasis becomes part of the care environment. CDC specifies disinfecting that chair and its armrests between patients.

column2: Which antibody pattern indicates natural immunity in an HBsAg-negative dialysis patient and ends routine HBV follow-up testing?
column7: Positive surface and core antibodies together indicate immunity following infection. Vaccine responders have surface antibody without core antibody and need periodic antibody monitoring.

column2: At closing, a wheelchair armrest is cracked and cannot be properly disinfected. Which status is appropriate for the chair?
column3: Unavailable until it can be repaired
column7: A cracked surface that cannot be adequately cleaned is unsuitable for shared use. Remove the wheelchair from service until its condition is corrected.

column2: During station turnover, which finding calls for an intermediate-level disinfectant after cleaning?
column5: Paper lint on the dialysate shelf
column7: Visible blood or body fluid calls for intermediate-level disinfection after soil removal. A hospital disinfectant appropriate for routine use suffices for station surfaces without that contamination.

column2: A visitor directly threatens clinic staff after declining an offer to talk privately. Which response fits this change in behavior?
column4: Continue de-escalation in a quiet room
column5: Have the charge nurse review the complaint
column6: Ask the team to clarify the waiting policy
column7: An explicit threat triggers the clinic's workplace violence response process. Ordinary service recovery and verbal discussion address a different level of concern.

column2: A community-wide exercise is inaccessible in the clinic's full-scale exercise year. Which substitute meets the federal requirement?
column7: A facility-based functional exercise substitutes in the year the community full-scale exercise is due. A tabletop exercise or workshop is available for the additional exercise in the alternate year.
